scope: Reader explanations, referenced maps and histories, and selected Design Horizon reading routes. Canonical graph unchanged.

design_horizon.title: Design Horizon
design_horizon.status: Live library and About inspected; eight relevant resource links selected; destination pages inspected. Full reading of every linked work and outcome evaluation are not claimed.

resources.title: Embedding Learning in Systems Change
resources.author: Kecia Bertermann and Julia Coffman
resources.date: Publication date not stated on the landing page
resources.locator: The Framework's Five Connected Elements; Download the Briefs
resources.summary: A framework connecting hypotheses, assumptions, learning questions, evidence and regular reflection to strategic decisions.
resources.question: What evidence would change your next decision?
resources.status: Source landing page inspected; six downloadable briefs are further reading.

resources.title: Systemic Design Framework
resources.author: Design Council
resources.date: Current resource page; publication date not stated
resources.locator: Systemic Design Framework; Systemic Design Toolkit; Designing for Legacy
resources.summary: A design framework that extends the Double Diamond to include relationships, leadership and continuing the work beyond a project.
resources.question: Which relationships and decisions sit outside the visible project process?
resources.status: Official framework page inspected; framework and toolkit marked CC BY 4.0.

resources.title: Design Justice Network Principles
resources.author: Design Justice Network
resources.summary: Ten principles about who shapes design decisions, community impact, facilitation and community control. The original principles remain at their source under CC BY-ND 4.0.
resources.question: Who can change the design, rather than merely comment on it?
resources.status: All ten principles inspected. The atlas comparison is editorial; no historical influence is asserted.

resources.title: Systems thinking for service design
resources.author: Yulia Besplemennova and Roberta Tassi
resources.locator: PDF pp. 1–4: repository citation, abstract and introduction
resources.summary: A working paper proposing changes to service-design tools so that they attend to changing behaviour, relationships and longer-term consequences.
resources.question: What would your service map show if you extended its timeframe?
resources.status: Repository citation, abstract and introductory argument inspected; full case-study evaluation remains open.

resources.title: UNDP Systems Portfolio Guide
resources.author: United Nations Development Programme
resources.date: Publication date not stated on the guide landing page
resources.locator: Guide landing page and resource navigation
resources.summary: A source route into UNDP's guidance and templates for organising work as a portfolio rather than a set of isolated projects.
resources.question: What could the initiatives learn from one another?
resources.status: Official guide route inspected; linked templates are further reading.

resources.title: Human Learning Systems: reports and guides
resources.author: Human Learning Systems community
resources.date: Collection of publications with separate dates
resources.summary: Reports and practical guides on public management that makes room for human relationships, learning and complex situations.
resources.question: How does evidence from people's lives change how a service is managed?
resources.status: Collection page inspected; individual reports need their own reading and assessment.

resources.title: Anindita's Story
resources.author: Saskia Rysenbry, Rachel Maria Taylor and Anna Birney / School of System Change
resources.date: Date not stated on the inspected page
resources.summary: A practitioner account of Anindita Ghosh's work with Q, connecting personal reflection, design and collaboration in health systems.
resources.question: How does a practitioner's own participation affect the change they seek?
resources.status: Published case account inspected; its account is not independent evidence of general effectiveness.

resources.title: Our Futures: By the people, for the people
resources.author: Laurie Smith and Kathy Smith / Nesta
resources.date: See report source for publication details
resources.locator: Report overview and participatory futures material
resources.summary: A report on involving people in imagining and shaping futures, with examples beyond conventional consultation.
resources.question: Whose future is being imagined, and who can act on it?
resources.status: Report overview inspected; full report and examples are further reading.

maps.title: Some Streams of Systemic Thought
maps.author: Eric Schwarz; extended for the International Institute for General Systems Studies
maps.locator: Streams of System Thought; May 2001 attribution
maps.summary: A broad genealogy joining philosophical, scientific and practical streams. Several differently named copies resolve to this same chart. Their filenames don't establish different authorship.
maps.status: Attribution and public ISSS source route checked; no diagram redistribution or automatic influence claims.

maps.title: History of the Ideas of Cybernetics and Systems Science
maps.author: Robert E. Horn, with contributions from Debora Hammond's students and ISSS participants
maps.locator: Mural information box; ISSS 50th anniversary, Sonoma State, 9–14 July 2006
maps.summary: A large historical mural combining people, quotations, publications and conferences. Two retained versions share this title; exact visual equivalence hasn't been established.
maps.status: Public account available. The original author-host PDF currently redirects to a suspended-host page; use the credited account rather than promising a working download.

maps.title: The Genesis of Complexity
maps.author: Ralph H. Abraham
maps.summary: A historical reconstruction relating cybernetics, general systems theory and system dynamics to complexity. The dates of the manuscript and published article are kept separate.
maps.status: Manuscript identity and publisher citation identified. This is Abraham's account of the history; its tree is not adopted as the atlas's final boundary.

maps.title: A Timeline for the Evolution of Cybernetics
maps.author: American Society for Cybernetics
maps.date: Undated historical web timeline; checked 13 October 2026
maps.locator: Opening explanation; Prehistory; Historical Era; other timelines
maps.summary: A chronological route through several strands contributing to cybernetics. The source explicitly describes its selection as incomplete.
maps.status: Official public timeline inspected. A timeline entry is a lead for checking history, not by itself a verified influence relationship.

maps.title: A Typology for the Systems Field
maps.author: David Rousseau, Jennifer Wilby, Julie Billingham and Stefan Blachfellner
maps.locator: Article citation; public SysCoI abstract; comparative-map figures and captions in the article
maps.summary: A published proposal for organising the systems field by its philosophies, theories and practices. It provides a public reference route for the systemology work and comparisons with earlier maps.
maps.status: Institutional publication record and public abstract checked. The separately retained confidential slide deck isn't reproduced or treated as public evidence.

maps.title: Field of Systems Thinking
maps.author: Clare Wright
maps.locator: Rousseau et al. (2016), comparative-map figure caption citing Wright (2012), p. 10
maps.summary: A developmental map reproduced and discussed in the published typology article. Attribution follows the figure caption; no separate live original has been verified.
maps.status: Referenced through the article; original publication and reproduction rights require further checking.

maps.title: Systems thinking and systems practice map
maps.author: Hans Georg Graf
maps.locator: Rousseau et al. (2016), discussion and caption for Graf's systemic-interests map
maps.summary: A comparison linking kinds of systems thinking and systems practice through systemic interests. The public article is the reference route; the historic interactive destination hasn't been verified.
maps.status: Bibliographic route identified; direct interactive map remains an access check.

maps.title: Four domains of the systems sciences
maps.author: Len Troncale
maps.locator: The systems sciences: What are they? Are they one, or many?, fig. 1; discussed in Rousseau et al. (2016)
maps.summary: A spectrum of general systems theories, disciplinary theories, systems analysis and applications. It is distinct from the Schwarz chart sometimes stored under a Troncale filename.
maps.status: Bibliographic comparator identified; original full-text and exact figure review remain open.

maps.title: A Taxonomy of Systems Science
maps.author: John van Gigch and Nic Kramer
maps.locator: Van Gigch and Kramer (1981), p. 183; reproduced in the comparative article material
maps.summary: A classification of systems science, useful for comparison with maps of historical influence. A classification and a genealogy answer different questions.
maps.status: Bibliographic comparator identified; original edition and exact reproduction remain to be checked.

maps.title: The shape of the systems movement
maps.author: Alexander Laszlo and Ervin Laszlo
maps.date: See chapter's bibliographic record; retained image has no reliable date
maps.locator: The Systems Sciences in Service of Humanity, section 4 and systems-movement diagram
maps.summary: A depiction of theoretical and applied branches within a wider account of systems sciences. Attribution comes from the public chapter, not from an ambiguous local filename.
maps.status: Public chapter and authors identified; no private image is reproduced.

maps.title: World of Systems and Systems Maps
maps.author: Peter Tuddenham; Streams of System Thought route with Marc Peirson / ISSS
maps.date: Systems Maps compiled 22 September 2017; living directory
maps.locator: Systems Maps; Streams of System Thought; attribution and source-connection caveat
maps.summary: A public directory and interactive reading routes that assemble many systems maps. A compiled collection isn't a single new map or a uniform source of evidence.
maps.status: Official directory inspected; its source-connection limitation is retained.

intake_limits: Fourteen retrieved non-correspondence files were inspected for identity. Duplicates were grouped; an image-only item was identified as E. T. Jaynes's Information Theory and Statistical Mechanics (1957), a paper rather than a field map.
Native folder enumeration failed; search retrieves text-friendly items, so unindexed files, images and subfolders cannot be certified as fully inventoried.
A restricted slide deck was excluded from public material; published systemology references were used instead.
This pass adds attributed reader routes. It does not import all diagram nodes or accept their historical relationships into the canonical graph.
